long_biography.plain_text:
An accomplished sports-car racer, Penske withdrew from competition to run a Philadelphia Chevrolet dealership financed with borrowed capital. From that base he built a disciplined acquisition and partnership model across vehicle retailing. He subsequently entered rental and full-service commercial fleets, adding contract maintenance, warehousing and supply-chain management. Those operations evolved into a global group spanning passenger-car showrooms, heavy-truck outlets and transport services.

Competition remained a parallel enterprise after he formed his own race team in 1966. Its programs expanded across American open-wheel, stock-car and endurance series, developing a record of championships and Indianapolis victories. Penske later brought the Speedway and the leading US open-wheel championship under a dedicated entertainment subsidiary. He continues directing both the operating companies and racing holdings, but dealership and fleet activities account for the larger commercial platform.
